answer: In a compute market serving a remote mesa, agents can whisper bids and wander between brokers, but each identity must lock collateral for 30 days, and its share of job assignments is proportional to that stake. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities earns no more total allocation than staking them under one name. To capture more jobs, an attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens, bearing their financing cost and price risk.
